dkbor: DMI's Bornholm radar sits on a former military tower on Rytterknægten, the island's highest point at 162 m, in the Almindingen forest. A radar has watched the Baltic Sea from here since 2007; after repeated breakdowns it was replaced by a new Vaisala radar in 2023.
dkrom: This DMI radar stands at Juvre on Rømø, a Wadden Sea island off south-west Jutland, and watches the German Bight and western Denmark. A radar has worked here since 1992; the current dual-polarisation unit was installed in 2017 as part of the renewal of the Danish network.
dksam: DMI's newest radar stands on a 20 m steel lattice tower just north of the village of Permelille on Samsø, an island in the middle of the Kattegat. Its 7 m dome went up in August 2023, and the radar took over from the old radar at Virring near Skanderborg; it reaches about 240 km.
dksin: DMI's northernmost radar stands near Sindal in Vendsyssel, the tip of Jutland, and covers the Skagerrak, the northern Kattegat and the coasts of Norway and Sweden. A radar has worked here since 1994; it was the first site to get a new dual-polarisation radar, in spring 2017.
dkste: This DMI radar stands at Mandehoved on the Stevns peninsula, next to a viewing tower near the chalk cliffs of Stevns Klint, a UNESCO World Heritage site. It covers Zealand, Copenhagen and the western Baltic; the current dual-polarisation radar replaced the earlier one in October 2017.
